post.title: Why CrowdStrike's stock fell after its $44B Zscaler deal
post.ig:
Why did CrowdStrike's stock fall after its roughly $44 billion deal?
CrowdStrike agreed Monday to buy Zscaler in an all-stock deal valued at about $43.9 billion, which reports call the largest cybersecurity deal on record.
Each Zscaler share becomes 1.135 CrowdStrike shares, a 34% premium based on Friday's closing prices.
Once the deal closes, current CrowdStrike owners would hold about 84.1% and Zscaler owners 15.9%. That's dilution.
Sources: CrowdStrike 8-K and press release (Nov 23, 2026), CNBC, TechCrunch.
